Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Gameplay 3 Milk 4 Scoring 4.1 Milk 4.2 Balance 4.3 Animals Objective Each player places animals in their two farms, red and blue, over 10 rounds to gain the most points. Gameplay During a round, dice (equal to the number of players +1) are rolled. On your turn pick a die and move a farmer meeple clockwise that number of spaces and collect the two animals depicted on the space that you land on. If you move the red farmer, you place the animals on your red farm. If you move the blue farmer, you place the animals on your blue farm. Farmers may not share the same space. If the number on the chosen die would land you on the other farmer's spot, you land one space farther. A round ends once each player has placed two animals. With the remaining die, rotate the top wheel clockwise the number of spaces equal to the die value. Milk You have the option to spend milk to change the number on the die to be a lower or higher number. Each player starts with 3 milk cartons and any milk remaining by the end of the game is 1 point each. Scoring The game ends after ten (10) rounds have been played. Note that you will not be able to fully fill up both of your farms. Milk 1 point per milk remaining Balance Aim to have an equal number of animals across your farms. Any difference in numbers is minus points. For example if you have 12 animals on your red farm and 8 animals on your blue farm, you will get -4 points. Animals Some animals are scored per farm: 1 pig = 1 point 2 pigs = 6 points (orthogonally adjacent) 1 sheep = 0 points 2 sheep = 2 points (orthogonally adjacent) 3 sheep = 12 points (orthogonally adjacent) Each chicken = 2 points Cows and calves (orthogonally adjacent) are multiplied, e.g. 2 cows x 4 calves = 8 points. (N.B. Calf tiles have 2 calves on them!), so this example is 2 cow tokens and 2 calf tokens. Other animals are scored across both farms: Whoever has most horses gets 10 points. The player with the second most gets 6 points (0 points in a 2-player game). In the case of a draw both players get 10 points and second place points do not apply. [Rating: 3/10] Basic roll and write game. Features a moving randomizing rondel gimmick that feels like it could easily be replaced by some far less convoluted animal selection mechanism, renders any kind of planning further than 'right now' moot, and on top is annoying to print and play. The initially most interesting part of balancing your two sub-sheets turned out to be of no big impact on final scores, and thus really not that interesting. Severly lacks nuclear tanks.

[Rating: 3/10] I guess it works but there are so many other better roll and writes out there...and it can be frustrating to have no good options when you are start player:)

[Rating: 5/10] This game combines a bunch of mechanisms that are perfectly serviceable but that I generally find produces an inoffensive but fairly run of the mill and dry game: set collection, drafting to get the set collection, and some additional spatial element for the set collection as well. This one adds a rondel and dice drafting, but I didn't feel like that changed up the decision space much; it was just another restriction. I don't think I ever want to play this again, but wouldn't mind it if it was just once in awhile.
